POC failing p99 under streaming with large context >8k tokens
notes: Context: mid-size fintech building a real-time chat assistant for traders + document search. Strong emphasis on tail latency for regulatory chat workflows.

Primary ask: definition and measurable alignment of latency SLOs across client/server boundaries (p50/p95/p99) and separate rules for streaming token latencies vs full-response non-streaming latencies.
Quote: "We care more about p99 for audit-facing flows — if the system spikes we get compliance alerts. p95 is acceptable for user-experience tradeoffs." — CTO (call 2026-02-10)

POC summary (Jan-Feb): ran synthetic workload against Redwood Dedicated trial (provisioned 4 x H100-equivalent nodes); baseline tests show:
  - Non-streaming: median end-to-end (client timestamp -> client response) ~45ms, p95 ~130ms, p99 ~320ms for 2k token responses
  - Streaming (per-token): server-inserted token latencies median ~12ms, p95 ~40ms, p99 ~95ms
  - Observed difference: client-side end-to-end includes LB/gateway + websocket framing (~20-50ms variance), server-only timings (arrival->send) ~30-60ms lower than client-side.

Key measurement discussion items:
  - Which signal is the SLO source of truth? Client-side end-to-end (user perceived) vs server-side ingress->egress. Solara favors client-side for UX but legal wants server-side logs for audit reproducibility.
  - Percentile window: 30d rolling preferred by Solara; Redwood recommends 7d for early detection + 30d for contractual SLA.
  - Streaming SLOs split: token-level tail (p99 token latency) + session-level completion time for long responses (>4k tokens).
  - Payload variance: large context (>8k tokens) amplifies KV-cache misses and increases p99 — need quantized model variant for reserved capacity fallback.

Throughput & reserved capacity planning:
  - Desired baseline throughput: 300 concurrent chat sessions peak (avg 40 qps), target sustained token throughput ~3M tokens/hour.
  - Redwood Dedicated proposal: 6x GPU nodes w/ autoscale headroom for bursts to 10 nodes. Solara wants guaranteed baseline throughput + documented behavior for autoscale/overcommit and cost for burst hours.
  - Acceptance criterion: no more than 2% request drop and p95 non-streaming under reserved baseline <= 150ms for standard prompts.

SLA negotiation points to surface to legal/procurement:
  - Clear definition of measurement (server vs client), measurement endpoints, and allowed measurement tools (synthetic harness vs production telemetry).
  - Remedies for SLA misses (service credits) and how burst capacity events are counted (do bursts outside reserved baseline count towards SLA?).
  - Security addenda: KMS integration timeline, SLA for audit log retention and export.
